cards.back: 1. For The Afterlife questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Link your discussion of The Afterlife to its real-world impact on believers and society
Eternal life with God; the beatific vision of God (e.g. Eternal life with God; perfect joy and peace)
Eternal separation from God; state of self-exclusion from God (e.g. Eternal separation from God; some believe in conscious torment, others in annihilation)
A state of purification before heaven; supported by 2 Maccabees 12:46 (e.g. Not accepted; Protestants believe Jesus' sacrifice fully cleanses all sin)
Particular judgement at death; final judgement at end of time (e.g. Judgement by God; emphasis on faith in Christ as the basis for salvation)

Students often confuse the Trinity as three gods rather than one God in three persons. Wrong: "Christians believe in three gods." Correct: "Christians believe in one God who exists as three persons — Father, Son and Holy Spirit."

cards.front: Understanding The Afterlife in Christian Practice
cards.back: The Afterlife is a key aspect of Christian practice that GCSE Religious Studies students must understand in depth. Christianity is the world’s largest religion with over 2 billion followers, and its practices shape the daily lives of believers. cards.front: Biblical and Theological Foundations of The Afterlife
cards.back: Christian practices are grounded in the Bible and developed through church tradition. cards.front: The Impact of The Afterlife on Christians Today
cards.back: Understanding the afterlife in the modern world means considering how Christians practice their faith in contemporary Britain and globally. Christianity in the UK is diverse: the Church of England (Anglican) is the established church, but there are also Catholic, Methodist, Baptist, Pentecostal and Orthodox communities, each with distinct approaches to the afterlife.
